newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Mar 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Mar 27.

text.p: There are 96 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The ECONOMIC JOURNAL said the Hong Kong government always interfered when the property market had reached a peak and was about to go down by itself anyway. The recent government measures to curb speculation had no significance apart from showing that the government was doing somethnng to control property prices, the paper said.

-- The Pro-Beijing WEN WEI PO China today was different from the way it was when the late U.S. President Richard Nixon paid his visit. China's rapid development had forced the United States to take it more seriously and adopt a pragmatic attitude when adjusting its China policies, the paper said.

--The English-language HONGKONG STANDARD said there had been some positive indications during the Beijing visit of U.S. Vice President Al Gore, including the signing of some lucrative contracts. The reconciliation process was just beginning. A strong, lasting relationship between the world's biggest country and richest country would augur well for international peace, it said.
